title: Energy-sector firms: eight alternatives, six criteria

source.citation: Biswas, S., Pamucar, D., Dawn, S., Simic, V. (2024). Evaluation based on Relative Utility and Nonlinear Standardization (ERUNS) method for comparing firm performance in energy sector. Decision Making Advances, 2(1), 1-21.
source.note: Open-access application co-authored by the method's second author. The original paper (Ecer and Pamucar 2022, Omega 112, 102690, doi:10.1016/j.omega.2022.102690) is paywalled; see docs/methods/lopcow.md.

notes: Criteria: C1 environmental score, C2 social score, C3 governance score, C4 debt-to-equity ratio (cost), C5 market capitalisation, C6 enterprise value (Tables 3-4).
Normalisation is min-max: (x - min)/(max - min) for benefit and (max - x)/(max - min) for cost criteria (Eqs. 10-11).
The "Mean Square" row is (1/m) sum_i r_ij^2; the percentage value is PV_j = |ln(sqrt(mean square) / sigma_j) * 100| (Eq. 12).

sigma_j is the sample standard deviation (divisor m - 1) of the normalised column. The population standard deviation gives P_j = 49.534, 77.066, ... and does not match; the paper only says "standard deviation", so this fixture is what fixes the convention.
